text:
se_harper: FYI a customer on Private VPC reported Prom metrics stopped arriving in our Grafana after they switched gateways. They see connection errors in their Prom remote_write logs. Any quick checks we should ping them to run?

sre_maya: Can you paste the remote_write stanza they're using? common issues are TLS mismatch, wrong endpoint/port, or SNAT from their NAT gateway blocking our collector IPs. :thinking_face:

se_harper: Here's what they sent (sanitized):
```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: "https://otlp-ingest.redwood-internal:4317/v1/prometheus"
    bearer_token: /var/run/secrets/token
    tls_config:
      insecure_skip_verify: false
```
They say connection refused from their side.

eng_jordan: 4317 is OTLP/gRPC port — Prom's remote_write usually expects HTTP remote write (default 9090) unless they use an OTLP-sidecar/adapter. Are they using promremotewrite-to-otlp adapter? If not, connection will fail.

se_harper: Good catch. I'll ask if they switched to OTLP adapter. Any quick dashboard/traces we can point them to?

platform_lee: Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/obs-CustVPC/customer-prom-metrics (read-only). For ingester health: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ingest/otlp-overview. Traces: Jaeger UI is at https://trace.redwood-internal/ (need VPN).

sre_maya: For logs+/debugging: ask them to curl the endpoint from a pod in their VPC:
```bash
kubectl run -it --rm debug --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never --namespace=default -- sh
# then inside pod
curl -v https://otlp-ingest.redwood-internal:4317/ || true
```
Expect TLS handshake if service speaks gRPC. If they get connection refused, check SG/NACL and their NAT. If TLS errors, confirm cert SANs and SNI.

se_harper: They replied: we get "connection refused" not TLS. Also their Prom logs show 503 for /api/v1/write.

eng_jordan: 503 for /api/v1/write suggests they're still sending HTTP remote_write to our HTTP ingest path, but the endpoint/port mismatch could cause adapter to reply 503. Ask them to run `promtool tsdb analyze` to confirm target config? Not necessary. Simpler: check the Prom remote_write url they actually hit (not what they think).

platform_lee: Also confirm their NAT IPs are whitelisted on our side — private customers usually have a set of egress IPs we expect. If gateway changed, IPs might not be permitted. I can check access logs on the ingesters; infra-bot, can you grep for recent connection attempts from that customer id?

infra-bot: Found 42 attempts from 10.4.22.13 at 2026-02-17T17:09:14Z -> connection refused. No TLS handshake recorded. Also several 503s from 192.168.11.7 hitting /api/v1/write at 2026-02-17T17:12:01Z.

sre_maya: So two distinct behaviors: some pods attempting gRPC (4317) and being refused; others hitting HTTP path and getting 503. Sounds like a misconfigured split deployment (sidecar vs direct). Ask them to confirm: are they using prom-to-otlp sidecar (otel-collector) or sending remote_write directly from Prom?

se_harper: I asked. They confirmed: they recently added an OpenTelemetry Collector that forwards Promremote -> OTLP but only in a subset of namespaces. The cluster-level Prom is still remote_writing directly to our HTTP ingest. They flipped a new gateway that blocks 9090 but allows 4317 egress.

eng_jordan: That explains it. Two actions for them:
  1) Update Prom remote_write to point to our HTTP ingest endpoint on expected port (e.g., https://prom-ingest.redwood-internal:443/api/v1/write) OR ensure OTLP adapter is properly in front of Prom.
  2) Ensure their VPC egress rules allow the required ports and SNAT range whitelisted in our swarm.

platform_lee: I'll share an onboarding snippet they can use for prom remote_write and relabeling:
```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: "https://ingest.redwood-internal/api/v1/write"
    remote_timeout: 30s
    queue_config:
      max_samples_per_send: 2000
    write_relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [__name__]
        regex: ".*"
        action: keep
```
Also recommend relabel to add a customer label: `- target_label: customer_id`

sre_maya: For alert tuning: their high-cardinality metrics were firing a ton of alerts. Recommend we temporarily raise alert suppression window and adjust threshold on `prometheus_remote_write_errors_total` to avoid noisy pages while they reconfigure. I can patch a customer-specific alert rule if you want.

se_harper: Please do, that'd stop pager fatigue. Set a 30m suppression and notify via the customer-case channel instead of oncall during business hours.

platform_lee: I'll open a PR against the customer alerting overlay with adjusted severity and suppression window. Will ping for review.

se_harper: Thanks all — I'll relay the prom vs otlp mismatch and the NAT IP whitelist step to the customer. Will follow up once they confirm. :white_check_mark:

sre_maya: If they still see issues after config change, ask them to collect tcpdump from a pod and we can inspect TLS handshakes. Example command: `tcpdump -i any host otlp-ingest.redwood-internal and port 4317`

se_harper: Noted. Closing loop once they confirm.
